clue.text: Roots of any really admirable, unusual clue and reliably intriguing answer produce a puzzling growth

indicators.note: the root of a word is taken here as where it starts, so each word gives up its opening letter

blocks.clueFragment: any really admirable, unusual clue and reliably intriguing answer
blocks.note: the opening letters of these nine words

explanation.surface: A setter's praise for a fine clue and its answer, which together make a satisfying puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: ARAUCARIA is the monkey puzzle tree, and also the pen name of a famous Guardian setter, which is why the surface praises admirable clues.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey puzzle tree belongs to the genus Araucaria, so a puzzling growth is a playful description of that plant.

clue.text: Duchess who divested new saint

blocks.note: the Duchess of Alba is said to have posed nude for Goya's Naked Maja
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A duchess who stripped off for a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divested' is part of the description of the duchess, the one who undressed for Goya; it gives no letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: St Alban is honoured as Britain's first Christian martyr, giving his name to the city of St Albans.

clue.text: Records are cut with knife

indicators.note: a cut opens something up, letting another piece be slipped into the gap

blocks.note: taken as written
chiv is old slang for a knife or blade

explanation.surface: Old documents are slashed with a blade.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a collection of historical documents, so it serves as a noun for records kept.

clue.text: Chinese brand getting fired with this?

blocks.note: first meaning: a seal or trademark stamped on goods in China and the Far East
second meaning: getting the sack is getting this

explanation.surface: Pottery is stamped with a maker's mark before going into the kiln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' suggests a kiln for the branded pottery; it means dismissed, as in getting the chop.
explanation.definitionFit: In the East a chop is an official stamp or mark of quality, and to get the chop is to be dismissed.

clue.text: Pride produced residual diet?

blocks.note: surface reading: arrogance leads someone to eat only leftovers
setter's reading: Colonel Pride purged Parliament in 1648, and the remnant left was an assembly, or diet

explanation.surface: Vanity makes a person live on scraps.
explanation.walkthrough: Pride's Purge expelled most members of the Long Parliament; what remained was nicknamed after the hind end, and a diet is a formal assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rump Parliament was the remnant left after the purge, and rump means a leftover remainder.

clue.text: Condition of confusing one's local with home, endlessly

indicators.note: to confuse is to muddle things, so all these letters are jumbled
without an end means the last letter of the word before is cut

blocks.note: one is I, with its 's
taken as written; in Britain a local is a pub
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone who treats the pub as home is in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British drinker's regular pub, which makes the surface nearly describe the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alcoholism is a medical disorder of dependence on drink, so it is a named illness or state of health.

clue.text: Principle of the characters in command

indicators.note: characters are just letters, so the word is broken down into its letters, to be set in any order

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in command, as in second-i/c

explanation.surface: A question about the guiding principle of the people who are in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethic is a moral rule or standard of conduct, so it is a synonym for a principle.

clue.text: "The law is the true ____" (Iolanthe), rendered by Eminem, Donny Osmond and Thomas Beecham initially

indicators.note: says only the opening letters of the two names are kept
rendered as in performed in a new version, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the rapper's name in full
the singer's initials
the conductor's initials

explanation.surface: A Gilbert and Sullivan lyric performed by an unlikely trio of a rapper, a pop star and a conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lord Chancellor in Iolanthe sings 'The law is the true embodiment of everything that's excellent'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word completes the famous Lord Chancellor's song in Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera.

clue.text: Quasimodo's premonitions?

blocks.note: surface reading: the bell-ringer's gut feelings about the future
setter's reading: the humps on the back of Hugo's hunchback of Notre-Dame

explanation.walkthrough: One word means both intuitions and humped shapes, and Quasimodo is famous for his hunched back.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuitive guesses about what will happen are gut feelings, and a hunchback's back has humps of that name.

clue.text: Revolutionary start to treatment in Spain for angina

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, the only one kept
one piece goes inside the following word

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary
first letter of treatment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A radical new therapy offered in Spain for a heart complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina pectoris is a heart condition felt as tightness and discomfort behind the breastbone.

clue.text: See 11
Oz player gets hit on the head

definitions.text: Oz player gets hit on the head

blocks.clueFragment: Oz player gets hit on the head
blocks.note: surface reading: an Australian sportsman takes a blow to the skull
setter's reading: the thing whose head is always struck, by a hammer; the metal Tin Man of The Wizard of Oz is perhaps the player meant

explanation.surface: An Australian sportsman takes a nasty knock to the skull.
explanation.walkthrough: The thing that is routinely hit on the head is the one a carpenter hammers in. 'Oz player' is the decoy; how the setter links it to the answer is not certain.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter drives this metal spike by striking its flat top with a hammer, again and again.

clue.text: Fame with hackney and hansom cabbies' chat, tho' it is dissipated!

annotation.answer: I HAD THAT WHATSHIS NAME IN THE BACK OF MY CAB ONCE

definitions.text: Fame with hackney and hansom cabbies' chat, tho' it is dissipated!

indicators.note: something dissipated is scattered and spent, so these words are broken up and their letters scattered

blocks.clueFragment: Fame with hackney and hansom cabbies' chat, tho' it
blocks.note: every letter of these ten words, forty in all

explanation.surface: Taxi drivers love to chatter about celebrity, though the fame fades as soon as it is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the stock boast of the London cabbie, who has always driven some celebrity whose name he cannot quite recall. Hackney carriages and hansoms are the old names for London cabs.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes the line: a cabbie's chat about fame, where the celebrity's name has evaporated, hence the dissipation.

clue.text: Serene, square and shorn!

blocks.note: S taken as short for square
shorn of tresses, with every lock of hair cut off

explanation.surface: A calm, conventional man with a shaved head.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone serene is calm and untroubled, free of anxiety or strain.

clue.text: No such infamy for limeys?

blocks.note: surface reading: a disgraceful reputation, meanness of character
setter's reading: British sailors ate limes to prevent the deficiency disease, so they were spared it

explanation.walkthrough: Limey is American slang for a Briton, from sailors given lime juice against scurvy; the answer means both shabby meanness and having that disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Scurvy as an adjective means contemptible, so the noun is a word for disgraceful meanness.

clue.text: Start to saute mushroom with a light touch: it sounds dubious

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept
says the last piece is wanted for how it is pronounced, not how the clue words read

blocks.note: opening letter of saute
the cep is the edible porcini mushroom
a tickle is a light touch; the word ending -tical is pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A cooking tip for frying mushrooms delicately, which the speaker doubts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sceptical means doubting or questioning, so it matches dubious in the sense of uncertain or unconvinced.

clue.text: Pish! Why ring the Lutine bell?

definitions.text: Pish! Why ring the Lutine bell?

blocks.clueFragment: Pish! Why ring the Lutine bell?
blocks.note: surface reading: an impatient question about pointless bell-ringing
setter's reading: the bell at Lloyd's of London was rung to announce a vessel lost at sea

explanation.walkthrough: The Lutine bell, from a frigate lost in 1799, hangs at Lloyd's of London insurers and was rung for news of a lost vessel. 'Pish' happens to rearrange to the first half.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the reason Lloyd's rang the bell: the loss of a vessel at sea.

clue.text: Nostradamus calling within: "Fly from the house!"

indicators.note: says the letters sit inside the run of words, spanning the gap between them

blocks.note: the end of the seer's name plus the start of the next word

explanation.surface: The prophet shouts from indoors, warning people to escape the building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like the verb flee; it is the insect. Musca domestica is the housefly, so 'from the house' points to domestica.
explanation.definitionFit: Musca is the zoological genus of the common housefly, whose full Latin name means domestic fly.

clue.text: See 11
Swinger seeking gin and the life of Riley, say?

indicators.note: say asks for the piece as it would be spoken out loud

blocks.note: a gin is a snare for animals
the life of Riley is an easy life

explanation.surface: A swinger looking for drink and a life of luxury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a partygoer; it is the circus bar. A gin here is not the drink but a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is the bar that acrobats swing from, so it is literally something that swings.

clue.text: Yen standard in ruins around thousands of Americans rioting

indicators.note: one set of letters is placed to surround the next before the mixing
rioting means running wild and out of order, so the combined letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: both words taken as written
a G or grand is American slang for a thousand dollars, so thousands are Gs

explanation.surface: The yen collapses as Americans riot in their thousands.
explanation.walkthrough: The flag of Japan, whose currency is the yen, shows a red sun; a standard is a flag, not a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rising Sun is the national flag of Japan, and a standard is a banner, so the flag of the yen's country.

clue.text: Lady of Shallot was half sick of Richard's old backers

definitions.text: Lady of Shallot was half sick of

blocks.clueFragment: Lady of Shallot was half sick of
blocks.note: first meaning: Tennyson's Lady of Shalott says 'I am half sick of' these
second meaning: Cliff Richard's backing band

explanation.walkthrough: The clue spells Shalott like the vegetable. Cliff Richard is a British pop singer whose original backing group shared the answer's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennyson's poem has the Lady weary of reflections in her mirror, and Cliff's band was called the Shadows.

clue.text: See 11
See 11
Early knights shouted the odds

indicators.note: shouted means the words are heard spoken, so their sound counts rather than spelling

blocks.note: knights spoken sounds like nights; early nights are evenings

explanation.surface: Medieval knights at a tournament calling out the betting.
explanation.walkthrough: Even is an old poetic word for evening.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookmaker's price where the stake is matched one for one is called evens.

clue.text: One might see a lot of such cars

definitions.text: One might see a lot of such cars

blocks.note: surface reading: a great many vehicles of some kind
setter's reading: a car lot, the forecourt where second-hand vehicles are sold

explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' reads as many; it is a dealer's forecourt full of second-hand cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand vehicles are previously owned, and dealers display them for sale on lots.

clue.text: Three kings succeeding bishop with a cold expression

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
R for rex, Latin for king, three times

explanation.surface: Three monarchs follow a bishop in procession, looking frosty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' tells us the kings come after the bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: The sound of shivering is written this way, an exclamation people make when freezing.

clue.text: El Greco, so sadly losing line, framing Mount Weizmann with "The Miser"

indicators.note: losing says one letter is dropped from the words before
sadly suggests things gone wrong and out of shape, so the letters are reworked
a frame surrounds a picture, so the reworked letters go round the next part

blocks.note: the painter's name and the following word as written
L is the abbreviation for line
ben is a Scottish mountain, as in Ben Nevis
Ezer Weizman was an Israeli president, nephew of Chaim Weizmann

explanation.surface: A sad El Greco painting of a mountain framed alongside a portrait called The Miser.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue spells Weizmann like Chaim, the first Israeli president; the piece wanted is the first name of his nephew Ezer Weizman, a later president. The shuffled letters split, one in front and the rest behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebenezer Scrooge is the tight-fisted hero of Dickens's A Christmas Carol, the archetypal skinflint.

clue.text: Capped for Ulster, are they?

blocks.note: surface reading: players picked to represent the Ulster team
setter's reading: the joints shot in punishment beatings by Northern Irish paramilitaries, known as kneecapping

explanation.surface: A question about which players have won caps for the Ulster side.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is Northern Ireland, where paramilitaries punished people by shooting the kneecaps; a sporting cap is the decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: The joints in the middle of the leg each carry a cap of bone, the patella, which is what gets capped.

clue.text: Disease of society is consuming Psyche and her lover

indicators.note: to consume is to take inside, so the first pair of pieces swallows the rest

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for society
taken as written
in Freud the id is part of the psyche
in myth Psyche was loved by Eros, or Cupid

explanation.surface: A society plagued by an obsession with Psyche and her lover Cupid.
explanation.definitionFit: Siderosis is a lung condition caused by inhaling iron dust, so it is a named illness.
